# R packages used in this book {#sec-packages}

R comes with a large set of functions, called *base R*. Most of the work in this book also uses *packages*, collections of functions written by others and shared freely, mostly through CRAN, the Comprehensive R Archive Network. @sec-packages-intro explains how packages are installed and loaded. This appendix lists all the packages used in the book, with a single command to install them.

## Packages by part {#sec-packages-list}

| Part | Packages | Used for |
|----------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Throughout | `tidyverse` (including `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `purrr`, `stringr`, `forcats`, `lubridate`, `ggplot2`, `tibble`) | Reading, transforming, reshaping and charting data |
| I. R Basics | `purrr`, `magrittr`, `conflicted` | Functional programming, the older pipe, and handling clashing function names |
| II. Getting and Shaping Data | `readxl`, `writexl`, `openxlsx`, `janitor`, `pdftools`, `tidyxl`, `unpivotr`, `data.table`, `duckdb`, `dbplyr` | Excel and PDF files, cleaning names, large data |
| III. Exploring, Statistics and Sampling | `scales`, `ggrepel`, `patchwork`, `psych`, `skimr`, `GGally`, `PerformanceAnalytics`, `broom` | Charts, descriptive statistics and tidy test results |
| IV. Working with Strings | `rebus`, `stringdist`, `phonics`, `PGRdup`, `cagmetaphone` | Regular expressions, string similarity and phonetic codes |
| V. Forensic Tests | `validate`, `pointblank`, `benford.analysis`, `bupaR`, `processmapR`, `edeaR`, `processcheckR` | Rule books, Benford's law, process mining |
| VI. Patterns and Anomalies | `broom`, `performance`, `car`, `moderndive`, `nnet`, `rpart`, `rpart.plot`, `ranger`, `cluster`, `factoextra`, `arules`, `forecast`, `timetk`, `zoo`, `outliers`, `AnomalyDetection`, `FNN`, `dbscan`, `isotree`, `changepoint`, `deaR` | Regression, classification, clustering, association rules, time series, anomalies and efficiency |
| VII. Text Analytics | `tidytext`, `SnowballC`, `wordcloud` | Words, sentiment and word clouds |
| VIII. Network Analytics | `igraph`, `igraphdata`, `ggraph`, `visNetwork` | Graphs and interactive networks |
| IX. Geospatial Analytics | `sf`, `leaflet`, `tidygeocoder` | Maps and geocoding |
| X. Reporting | `gt`, `openxlsx`, `quarto` | Formatted tables, Excel working papers, rendering reports |
| Appendices | `RColorBrewer`, `colorspace`, `palmerpenguins` | Colour palettes, and an example dataset |

: Packages used in each part of the book {#tbl-packages}

`MASS`, `lattice` and `nnet`, also used in the book, come with every installation of R and need no separate installation.

## Installing all the packages {#sec-packages-install}

The following command installs every CRAN package used in the book. It needs an internet connection, and may take a while the first time. If your office network blocks downloads, see the note on installing packages on an office network in @sec-packages-intro.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "conflicted", "readxl", "writexl", "openxlsx", "janitor",
  "pdftools", "tidyxl", "unpivotr", "data.table", "duckdb", "dbplyr",
  "scales", "ggrepel", "patchwork", "psych", "skimr", "GGally", "PerformanceAnalytics", "broom",
  "rebus", "stringdist", "phonics", "PGRdup",
  "validate", "pointblank", "benford.analysis", "bupaR", "processmapR", "edeaR", "processcheckR",
  "performance", "car", "moderndive", "rpart", "rpart.plot", "ranger", "cluster", "factoextra",
  "arules", "forecast", "timetk", "zoo", "outliers", "FNN", "dbscan", "isotree", "changepoint", "deaR",
  "tidytext", "SnowballC", "wordcloud",
  "igraph", "igraphdata", "ggraph", "visNetwork",
  "sf", "leaflet", "tidygeocoder",
  "gt", "quarto", "RColorBrewer", "colorspace", "palmerpenguins", "remotes"
))
```
:::


Two packages are not on CRAN, and are installed from GitHub with the package `remotes`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Double Metaphone with full-length codes, by Atharv Tyagi
remotes::install_github("AtharvTyagi1805/cagmetaphone")
# Seasonal Hybrid ESD anomaly detection, by Twitter
remotes::install_github("twitter/AnomalyDetection")
```
:::


The first of these, a full implementation of the Double Metaphone algorithm keeping phonetic codes of up to 32 characters, was developed by Atharv Tyagi during an internship under the author's guidance. It is used in @sec-strsim, @sec-dup and @sec-linkage.

::: callout-tip
## Keeping an analysis reproducible

Packages are updated from time to time, and occasionally a function changes its behaviour. For an audit that must be reproducible, record the versions used, as shown in @sec-TIDYVE with `sessionInfo()`. For larger projects, the package `renv` keeps a separate, fixed set of package versions for each project, so that an analysis written today runs the same way next year.
:::
